doc.title: Bucky Pizzarelli interviewed by Monk Rowe, Aspen, Colorado, October 11, 1997 [interview 1 of 2]

chapter: New York studio and TV work
title: Studio money, jazz gigs on the side, and meeting Goodman
summary: Studio work paid well, he played weekend trio jobs in Jersey for $35-40, and Goodman then changed everything.

story.theme_name: Making a living: hard times, day jobs and scarce work
story.community_name: Getting paid: wages, scale and the pay envelope

blocks.x: How did you guys feel about this music?

Well we were making money you know, and we could play gigs at night, but we got so busy we had no time to play gigs, no time. But I used to do, on Fridays and Saturdays, I played over in Jersey with a trio — piano, bass and guitar — all the time. I always had a little thing like that going on the side.

Well not to keep them but I just did it automatically because I felt that this is what I like to do so I’ll make some money and support the family and everything doing the recordings, and go play for — I don’t know it was $35 or $40 a night to play that kind of music.
Keeps things in perspective I suppose. And you had a family by this time.
Oh yeah. We were all grown up and I tried to make it work you know, but then in the middle of that whole thing I got hooked up with Benny Goodman you know. And that changed everything around.
